text:
monitoring-bot: ALERT SLO burn: hosted-inference / us-central p99 latency 2.8s (SLO=1s), p50 ok. spike started ~10:12 UTC, error rate (5xx) up 4x. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/hosted/infer/us-central — runbook link: https://runbooks/redwood/slo-burn

alice: seeing this now, paging oncall. any customer escalations?

carla: support-oncall reported two customers having increased 5xxs and timeouts starting 10:10. they saw client-side retries piling up. forwarding snippets from customer A: `curl` to /v1/generate returning 502 and occasional `upstream timeout` in body.

ben: quick check - datadog query shows spike in `gateway.request_duration{env:prod,region:us-central}.p99` and a correlated bump in `proxy.conn_reset` and `connector.queue_depth`. suspect connector-side backlog rather than model compute.

alice: can you paste the log query? I want to check traces.

ben: log query I used (loki style):
```
{app="gateway"} |= "upstream timeout" | json | duration > 500
| sort by @timestamp desc | limit 50
```
Most upstream timeouts point to `connector-async` with logs: `WARN connector-async: queue full, rejecting request`

support-oncall: customer A says their requests start getting 429 then 502 after retries. They disabled client retries and error rate dropped for them, but platform still shows p99 high.

dave: that pattern looks like connector throttling cascading into gateway timeouts. Did we deploy anything to connector/ingress in the last hour?

alice: deployment history shows a config change at 09:58 to connection-pool defaults (max_idle=8 -> 4) for connector pods. change author: infra/steve.

carla: oh right — that pool change was pushed as an optimization. If connectors close idle handles sooner, under bursty traffic we might hit short-term exhaustion and queue growth. customers with retries could make it worse.

ben: confirm: traces show many requests end at gateway with no downstream spans -> TRACE GAP. sampling didn't change, looks like requests never reached model pod before timeout.

alice: quick mitigation plan: 1) roll back connector pool change, 2) enable temporary rate-limiter increase for customer tier to absorb retries? 3) add short-term throttling at edge to smooth bursts. anyone object?

dave: +1 for rollback, rolling out now. I'll bump pool to previous 8 on connector autoscaling group.

ben: patch applied to connector config in us-central canary. watching metrics.

monitoring-bot: NOTICE config rollback triggered by alice at 10:26 UTC. watch SLOs for next 20m.

support-oncall: told customer A we rolled something back and to re-enable normal retry behavior in 15m. they appreciate the update. :thumbsup:

alice: after rollback p99 dropped to ~0.9s at 10:34, 5xxs down to baseline. still seeing a few `queue full` WARNs but much less frequent.

ben: follow-ups: - add a dashboard tile for `connector.queue_depth` and `connector.idle_conns` with alerting threshold, - add trace sampling at gateway to surface pre-connector spans even for timeouts, - add a chaos test that exercises connector pool saturation.

carla: support items: document recommended client retry strategy (exponential backoff + jitter) and include guidance to disable aggressive retries during incidents. link to doc sent to customer.

alice: creating incident ticket INC-2026-195 with timeline, root cause: connector connection-pool reduction + client retry storm -> queue saturation -> gateway timeouts (trace gaps). Owner: dave.

dave: on it. I'll also add a small safety guard in connector to log stack traces when `queue full` hits threshold and emit a synthetic span so we don't lose the trace next time.

support-oncall: closing the customer escalation for now; will reopen if customer sees recurrence.

ben: adding TODOs to infra backlog: revert risky pool tuning without load ramp, improve observability for pre-downstream handoff metrics, add canary test for pool config changes.

alice: thanks team — nice rapid triage. Marking this thread resolved but keep an eye on US-CENTRAL for 2 hours. :eyes:
